title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Claire Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls for: role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, centralized audit logging, data residency and retention policies, a secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the process for documented risk and exception handling. It is intended for security, platform, infra, SRE, and engineering teams responsible for builders and operators of the Redwood inference platform and private deployments.

Scope

- Applies to: Redwood hosted control plane, Dedicated customer pools, Private (VPC/on-prem) control plane, telemetry and audit pipelines, and developer tooling (console, APIs, SDKs).
- Excludes: personal devices external to BYOD policy and third-party vendor-internal systems (see vendor risk policy).

High-level goals

1. Ensure least-privilege access across services and deployments.
2. Capture tamper-evident audit trails for security-sensitive actions.
3. Enforce data residency and retention consistent with contracts and regulations.
4. Integrate security gates in the SDLC to prevent regressions.
5. Provide repeatable, auditable evidence packages for compliance assessments.
6. Maintain a clear, documented exceptions process with risk acceptance.

Roles & responsibilities

- Security (owner): policy authoring, oversight, control validation, compliance packaging.
- Eng-Platform/Infra: implement RBAC mappings, SSO, log forwarding, runbooks.
- Eng-SRE: monitoring, incident response coordination, retention enforcement.
- Product/Legal: data residency and contract-specific requirements.
- Customer Success/Support: execute access approvals for customer-supported private deployments.

RBAC & Authentication

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; role separation for admin, operator, developer, and auditor functions.
- No permanent root; short-lived elevation (just-in-time) for emergency actions.
- Centralized SSO + SCIM provisioning for identity lifecycle.
- MFA required for all interactive sessions and console access; service accounts use short-lived tokens tied to KMS-wrapped keys.

Canonical roles (examples):
- system-admin: full platform control; reserved for cloud operations and platform security engineers.
- org-admin: management of org-level billing, quota, and user invites; restricted to product/finance-approved roles.
- model-operator: deploy/rollback model-serving configurations and routing policies.
- infra-operator: manage GPU pools, autoscaling policies, and capacity.
- security-auditor: read-only access to audit logs, config, and event traces.
- developer: create models, prompts, and non-production routes.
- support-agent: access to customer tickets and limited session replay (redacted PII).

Implementation standards:
- Identity provider: SAML 2.0 + OIDC with SCIM for provisioning. Primary IdP is Okta (enterprise customers may use their IdP for private deployments).
- Service-to-service: mTLS for internal RPCs; JWT tokens issued by internal STS with 1 hour default TTL.
- Emergency elevation: GitHub PR-based request + approval by two system-admins recorded in the audit log; elevation limited to 1 hour.
- IAM policy examples and minimal permission sets are in Appendix A.

Authentication & secrets:
- KMS-backed secrets for all environment-level keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / customer HSM in private).
- Rotate long-lived credentials quarterly; prefer ephemeral credentials via STS.

Audit Logging

Objectives:
- Capture immutable, tamper-evident logs for security-relevant events: authentication, role changes, config changes, model deploys, billing access, and data export actions.
- Centralize logs to a hardened store with access controls and integrity mechanisms.

Log categories and retention:
- Auth logs (SSO sign-ins, MFA events): retention 2 years (compliance default).
- Admin & config change logs (IAM changes, routing policies): 7 years (for enterprise/regulatory customers) or 1 year default.
- Access logs (API requests, console actions): 365 days.
- Audit pipeline metadata (ingest/forwarding health): 90 days.

Log pipeline architecture (summary):
1. Agents (service-side) emit structured JSON events with standardized fields: timestamp, service, principal_id, action, resource, request_id, trace_id, outcome, and change_before/after (redacted).
2. Events are forwarded via the audit-forwarder service to the central log cluster (immutable buckets + append-only index).
3. Integrity: periodic hash chaining and signed manifests are published to an internal transparency bucket to detect tampering.
4. Retention enforcement jobs run daily to enforce policy and escalate any drift.

Access & monitoring:
- Only security-auditor role and designated SREs have read access to raw audit logs.
- Support leads get redacted views for troubleshooting.
- Alerting: suspicious activities (mass role changes, multiple failed SSO logins, export of >1000 records) trigger P1 alerts to oncall and security.

Example audit event (text):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-15T14:32:22Z",
  "service": "control-plane",
  "principal_id": "alice@redwood.com",
  "action": "grant-role",
  "resource": "org:acme-corp",
  "request_id": "req_12345",
  "outcome": "success"
}

Data Residency & Retention

Policy summary:
- Data classification: PII, Customer Data (non-PII), System Telemetry, Audit Logs.
- Residency commitments are contract-driven (e.g., EU-only regions for EU customers).
- Default residency: multi-region within customer-chosen jurisdiction (e.g., us-west-2 + us-east-1) for resilience unless customer requests single-region.
- Cross-border transfer: disabled by default for restricted customers; any transfer must be documented and approved by legal.

Retention defaults and encryption:
- Customer content (prompts, responses): default retention 90 days for hosted; configurable per-customer (min 0 days).
- Embeddings & model logs: default 180 days for inference telemetry; longer retention negotiated.
- Audit logs: see Audit Logging section.
- All data at rest encrypted with platform-managed KMS keys; customers may supply BYOK (bring-your-own-key) in Private deployments.

Data access controls:
- Data-in-transit: TLS 1.2+ (prefer TLS 1.3).
- Data-at-rest: AES-256 with CMKs.
- Access to customer content restricted via organization-scoped IAM policies and logged to audit pipeline.

Data deletion & eDiscovery:
- Standard process for deletion requests: ticket creation (support), verification of identity/authorization, backend purge job, and audit entry.
- eDiscovery/Legal hold: suspend retention deletion jobs for specified org_id and preserve artifacts in a legal-hold bucket.

Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)

Security gates & tooling:
- Threat modeling: mandatory for all public-facing services and any change >2 microservices.
- Code review: 2 approvers minimum, at least one from security for high-risk changes.
- Static Analysis (SAST) and Dependency Scanning: must run in CI and block merges on critical or high alerts.
- Secrets scanning: must run in pre-merge and periodic repository scans.
- Container scanning and SBOM generation on release.
- Runtime protection: eBPF-based anomaly detection for host-level behavior in Dedicated clusters.

Release policy & environment segregation:
- Environments: dev -> staging -> pre-prod -> prod. Promotion requires passing security smoke tests, integration tests, and canary rollout plan.
- Canary & rollout: default 5% traffic canary for 24 hours unless a service is high-risk; automatic rollback on error budget breach or SLO regression.

Third-party & open source controls:
- Approved OSS list and dependency risk register maintained by security.
- New third-party services require vendor risk assessment and a contract addendum if handling customer data.

Incident Response Security Procedures

Objectives:
- Ensure rapid detection, containment, eradication, and recovery from security incidents.
- Preserve forensic evidence and produce post-incident reports for stakeholders.

Incident classification & SLA (security-specific):
- Sev 0 / P0 (active exfiltration, cluster compromise): detection to acknowledgment <= 15 minutes; containment plan within 60 minutes; executive notif within 2 hours.
- Sev 1 / P1 (sensitive data exposure, major outage with security implications): detection to ack <= 30 minutes; containment within 4 hours.
- Sev 2 / P2 (unauthorized access to non-sensitive resources): detection to ack <= 4 hours.

Playbook summary (for a suspected data exfiltration):
1. Triage & contain: isolate affected compute nodes, revoke implicated tokens, and rotate service keys.
2. Forensics: snapshot disks, preserve memory if possible, and collect relevant audit logs and network flows.
3. Notification: trigger legal, privacy, and affected customer notification process per contracted timelines.
4. Remediation: patch vulnerability, rebuild affected services, validate via integration tests and smoke tests.
5. Postmortem: security-led postmortem within 7 calendar days; include root cause, timeline, impact, and remediation actions.

Evidence preservation:
- Forensic artifacts stored in an immutable evidence bucket with restricted access.
- Chain-of-custody ticket for any physical media if applicable.

Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose: provide reproducible evidence bundles for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, regional regulations).

Standard evidence package contents:
- Control descriptions and mapped owner(s).
- Access control listings (RBAC exports) with timestamps.
- Audit log extracts associated with control assertions (hashed manifests).
- Policy documents: data residency and retention declarations for the customer in scope.
- SDLC artifacts: PR reviews, SAST and dependency scan results, release notes.
- Incident log (if relevant) and remediation records.

Request & fulfillment process:
1. Request via compliance portal (ticket).
2. Evidence owner assigned (security).
3. Automated exports generated from config DB and audit store; manual corroboration by owners.
4. Package reviewed and signed by security lead; delivery via secure file share with expiration.

Retention of evidence packages: minimum 7 years for enterprise contracts; 1 year default for routine requests.

Risk & Exceptions

Exception process:
- All exceptions to security policy require an exception request ticket with: risk statement, compensating controls, TTL (max 90 days), and business justification.
- Approval path: owner-team manager -> security reviewer -> CISO for high-risk exceptions.
- Exception metadata recorded in the exception registry and exported monthly to the audit pipeline.

Compensating controls examples:
- Temporary network isolation + granular firewall rules.
- Enhanced monitoring & increased log retention for impacted resources.
- Time-limited privileged access with mandatory session recording.

Risk acceptance thresholds:
- Low: documented with manager approval.
- Medium: security reviewer + manager.
- High: CISO + risk committee and exec sponsor.

Operational runbooks (quick references)

- RBAC change request runbook: Steps to approve and implement role changes, including CLI commands, rollback, and audit verification.
- Audit log ingestion failure: diagnose forwarder, requeue pipeline, temporary retention extension.
- Data deletion request: identity verification checklist, backend purge command, verification steps.
- Incident containment: immediate token revocation commands and standard containment checklist.

Appendices

Appendix A - Minimal IAM policy samples (text):
- security-auditor (read-only):
  Actions: ["audit:ReadEvents", "config:Get*", "logs:Query*"]
  Resources: ["arn:redwood:audit:*:*:events/*"]

- model-operator:
  Actions: ["serving:DeployModel", "serving:RollbackModel", "serving:ReadModelConfig"]
  Resources: ["arn:redwood:serving:*:*:models/*"]

Appendix B - Retention table (human-readable):
- Customer content: default 90 days (configurable)
- Embeddings & telemetry: default 180 days
- Auth logs: 2 years
- Admin changes: 7 years (enterprise) / 1 year (default)
- Audit pipeline metadata: 90 days

Appendix C - Sample CLI snippets (text):
- Revoke user session (example):
  redwood auth revoke-session --user alice@redwood.com --reason "suspected compromise"

- Export RBAC snapshot:
  redwood admin export-rbac --org acme-corp --out rbac-acme-2026-01-15.json

Appendix D - Evidence checklist (short):
- [ ] RBAC export for period
- [ ] Signed policy documents
- [ ] Audit log hashes and manifest
- [ ] SDLC artifacts (PRs, scans)
- [ ] Incident records (if applicable)

Maintenance & review cadence

- Security team will review and update this document at least quarterly or after any major incident or compliance change.
- Annual tabletop exercise covering RBAC compromise and data residency misconfiguration.

Contacts & escalation

- Security oncall: security-oncall@redwood.com (pageable)
- Incident commander runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Compliance evidence requests: compliance-requests@redwood.com
